        return HANumber("number.xtouch_living_room_encoder")

    @haad_ha_entity
    def buttons(self) -> HAEventEntity:
        return HAEventEntity("event.xtouch_living_room_buttons")

    @haad_ha_entity
    def light(self) -> HALight:
        return HALight("light.living_room")

    @haad_ha_entity
    def speaker(self) -> HAMediaPlayer:
        return HAMediaPlayer("media_player.living_room")

    async def initialize(self) -> None:
        async def dim() -> None:
            # turn_on() of HALight does nothing for a light that is on: set the brightness directly
            brightness = await self.fader.get_state()
            await self.ha.perform_action("light/turn_on", entity_id=self.light.entity_id, brightness_pct=brightness)

        async def volume() -> None:
            await self.speaker.volume_set(await self.encoder.get_state() / 100)

        async def button() -> None:
            if await self.buttons.get_event_type() == "mute_pressed":
                await self.light.toggle()

        await self.react_to(trigger=self.fader, action=dim)
        await self.react_to(trigger=self.encoder, action=volume)
        await self.react_to(trigger=self.buttons, action=button)

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Start with the log and the state of the service:

systemctl --user status xtouch-daemon      # is the device, the sound server, the broker connected?
journalctl --user -u xtouch-daemon -f      # the log

For more detail, stop the service and run the daemon in the foreground with xtouch-daemon run -l debug.

items.title: The device
items.text:
The device shows IP: 192.168.001.100 wait.... It is set to its network interface and ignores USB. Switch it to MC mode on USB in its setup menu, see Getting started.

... is it switched on, in MC mode on USB? xtouch-daemon test can't find the sound card of the extender. The daemon waits for it and connects when it appears. Check that it is connected and on, and that /proc/asound/cards lists it. If the name differs, set [device] name to a part of it.

can't open X-Touch-Ext (... Device or resource busy). Only one program can use the device. Stop the daemon before xtouch-daemon test (systemctl --user stop xtouch-daemon), and close DAWs or other MIDI tools that opened it.

... Permission denied. Your user can't open the MIDI device in /dev/snd. Desktop sessions give access to the logged-in user; without a session, add the user to the audio group. See Hardware.

A fader does not change the volume. Only a touched fader changes a value. A fader whose touch sensor failed goes back to its value after a move. xtouch-daemon test shows whether the device reports fader touched. Until the sensor is repaired, touchless_faders makes the fader work without it.

A fader jumps on its first move after the daemon started. The device can't tell where its faders are, so after a connect the daemon assumes them at the bottom. A fader moved while the daemon did not run jumps from where it really is. See Hardware.

items.title: Audio
items.text:
The meters stay dark. A meter shows a level only while something plays to the output or records from the input. That is on purpose: the meters never open a device themselves. A microphone meter moves only while an application records from it. Check also behavior.meters and the strip's meter.

Streams don't follow when I select another output. Select makes the device the default, and streams without a fixed target follow the default. A stream that another tool moved to a particular device (pavucontrol's per-stream output menu, pactl move-sink-input) stays there. Move it back in pavucontrol, or restart the application's stream.

A strip shows off. The device it controls is not there, e.g. Bluetooth headphones that are switched off. It comes back by itself. xtouch-daemon list-devices shows the devices that are there.

An apps strip shows idle. No stream of its applications is there. xtouch-daemon list-apps shows the names and binaries of the applications that play, and which strip takes each one.

Select does not start the application of launch. The daemon's log says why: a program that is not in PATH (can't launch ...), or one that did not show up in 15 s. Nothing happens either while the strip counts it as running: on apps strips also a process whose name contains a match entry (ps -eo comm shows them). The application's own output is in journalctl --user -u 'xtouch-launch-*'. A graphical application that finds no display there needs the desktop's variables in the systemd user manager (systemctl --user show-environment should list WAYLAND_DISPLAY or DISPLAY); most desktops import them at login.

An application lands on the wrong strip. xtouch-daemon list-apps names the strip that takes it. An apps strip takes every application whose name or binary contains one of its match entries, so a short entry can match more than intended. check-config shows what the presets in match stand for.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: A change does not show on the device. Reload the daemon after saving: systemctl --user reload xtouch-daemon. A file with errors is logged and the old configuration stays: run xtouch-daemon check-config. A changed [device] name or [mqtt] section needs a restart. The GUI tells whether the device runs the saved file.

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text:
The entities are unavailable. They are available only while the daemon runs and the device is connected. Check the broker settings in [mqtt] and the log. The GUI tells how the connection is doing next to the preview and on the page "Home Assistant", where "Test connection" tries the settings.

A strip shows offline. The broker can't be reached. The daemon connects again by itself.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
xtouch-daemon reads a TOML file, by default ~/.config/xtouch-daemon/config.toml ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME is respected). -c FILE selects another one. Without a file at the default path it uses the example configuration: six auto strips, the default input and the default output.

xtouch-daemon init-config      # writes the example to the default path (-f overwrites)
xtouch-daemon check-config     # validates the file and lists what each strip does

Unknown options are errors, so a typo does not go unnoticed. check-config names the place of every error, e.g. strip[3].label: String should have at most 7 characters.

The GUI edits the same options in a window and shows the same errors next to them.

items.title: Sections
items.text:
Section What it configures Page [device] Which sound card is the extender. Behavior [behavior] Volume limit, encoder step, reset volume, meters, auto strips, collapsing strips. Behavior [aliases] Names to show for applications on auto strips. Behavior [[strip]] Up to eight strips, from the left (more with collapse). Strips [mqtt] The MQTT broker of Home Assistant. Home Assistant

The strip types:

type What the strip controls Page output, input An output or an input device, several of them, choices to switch between, or the default one. Devices apps All streams of a group of applications. Applications auto The next application that plays and has no strip of its own. Applications homeassistant Nothing by itself: its parts are entities in Home Assistant. Home Assistant empty Nothing. A dark strip. Strips

items.title: Applying changes
items.text:
xtouch-daemon check-config && systemctl --user reload xtouch-daemon

A reload (SIGHUP) builds the strips from the new file without a restart. A file with errors is reported in the log and the current configuration stays.

Two sections need a restart (systemctl --user restart xtouch-daemon):

  • A changed [device] name. A reload takes the rest of the file, but keeps the old device.
  • A changed [mqtt] section. Until the restart, a reload keeps the whole current configuration.

The GUI applies a saved file the same way: it reloads the running daemon (the service, or one started from a terminal or an IDE), or offers a restart. It then tells whether the daemon took the file.

items.title: Complete example
items.text:
[behavior]
max_volume = 130
encoder_step = 2
auto_hold = 10
ignore = ["speech-dispatcher", "notification"]

[aliases]
"WEBRTC VoiceEngine" = "Discord"

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
label = "Speaker"
color = "cyan"

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "bluez_output.4C_D7_3A_EA_02_76.1"
label = "Buds"
color = "green"

[[strip]]
type = "input"
label = "Mic"
color = "red"

[[strip]]
type = "apps"
match = ["@browsers"]
label = "Browser"
color = "yellow"

[[strip]]
type = "apps"
match = ["@games"]
label = "Games"
color = "magenta"

[[strip]]
type = "empty"

# strips 7 and 8 are not configured: they are "auto" strips

items.title: Applications: apps and auto strips
items.text: Application strips control the playback streams of applications, like the per-application sliders in pavucontrol. They need no setup in PipeWire.

items.title: apps strips
items.text:
All playback streams of a group of applications.

Option Default Meaning type required "apps". match required Parts of application names or binaries, ignoring case, or presets like "@browsers". label required The top line of the LCD. encoder "media" media, volume, balance or homeassistant, see Encoders. launch none A command that Select starts while none of the applications runs, see Launching the application. launch_when_running false Select starts launch also while the application runs.

They also have the options of every audio strip: color, meter, rec, solo, min_volume, max_volume, fader, id.

[[strip]]
type = "apps"
match = ["@voip"]
label = "VoIP"
color = "white"

A stream belongs to the strip when its application name (application.name) or binary (application.process.binary) contains one of the match entries. "wine" matches wine64-preloader, ".exe" matches Windows games under Proton. xtouch-daemon list-apps shows the names and binaries of the applications that play, and which strip takes each one. A stream can belong to several apps strips.

For common groups there are presets: @browsers, @voip, @games, @steam-games, @music and @video stand for the names of well-known applications of the group, e.g. match = ["@browsers"] for every browser, and mix with names of your own (match = ["@voip", "my-voice-app"]).

Element Function Fader Sets every stream of the group to the same volume. A stream that starts later gets that volume too. Shows the loudest stream. Encoder See Encoders, for all streams. Mute Mutes all streams, or unmutes them when all are muted. The LED is on while all are muted. Select Nothing, or with launch it starts the application. The LED flashes while it starts and is on while it runs, see Launching the application. LCD Top: the label. Bottom: the volume, muted, or idle while no stream of the group is there. Ring What the encoder controls. Meter The level of all streams of the group together.

While no stream of the group is there (e.g. the application was closed), the LCD is dark and shows idle, and the fader glides slowly to the bottom and does nothing. The strip keeps its volume while the daemon runs: when a stream comes back, the fader goes up to it and the stream gets it.

items.title: auto strips
items.text:
The next application that plays and has no strip of its own.

Option Default Meaning type required "auto". encoder "pick" pick, media, volume, balance or homeassistant, see Encoders. launch, launch_when_running none, false Like on apps strips: Select starts a command while the strip has no application.

They also have the options of every audio strip. There is no label: the label is the application's alias from [aliases], or its name.

[[strip]]
type = "auto"
color = "cyan"

How auto strips get their applications:

  • An application qualifies while at least one of its streams plays (is not paused).
  • Applications that an apps strip matches, and applications in behavior.ignore, never go to auto strips.
  • Free auto strips take new applications from the left, in the order the applications started.
  • An application keeps its strip while it plays, and for behavior.auto_hold seconds after it stopped. Then the strip is free again. This way a music player does not jump to another strip between two tracks.
  • A newly assigned application keeps its own volume.

With the default encoder = "pick", the encoder chooses the application and a push pins it, so it stays after it stopped playing. See Encoders.

An auto strip works like an apps strip for its application. Without an application it is dark, blank, and does nothing.

items.title: Launching the application
items.text:
With launch, the Select button of an apps, auto or voip strip starts an application while it does not run: the voice chat, the music player.

[[strip]]
type = "apps"
match = ["@voip"]
label = "VoIP"
color = "yellow"
lit_when_idle = true
launch = ["mumble", "mumble://markus@voice.example.org/Gaming"]
  • launch is the program and its arguments, as a list. It never runs through a shell: no ~, $VARIABLES, pipes or &&. A single string works too (launch = "mumble mumble://markus@voice.example.org/Gaming") and is split like a shell splits it, with quotes, but nothing is expanded.
  • Select starts it only while none of the strip's applications runs:
    • apps: no stream matches match, and no process whose name contains one of the match entries runs (like the processes rule), so a silent voice chat counts as running. For a preset, its processes count, e.g. Steam's reaper for @steam-games.
    • auto: the strip has no application.
    • voip: the voice chat is not there (its plugin does not report).
    • On all of them, a process named like the program of launch (the file name of its first part, exactly) counts too.
  • While it runs, Select does nothing (on voip strips of the group it pages, as before). With launch_when_running = true (apps and auto strips) Select starts the command also then.
  • The Select LED flashes while the application starts (until it runs, at most 15 s), then it is on while it runs. On voip strips of the group it is on while there are more participants than strips, as before. The voip strips of a layout with the same command start it once.
  • A second press within 5 s while the application is not up yet does nothing.
  • The application runs on its own: as a transient systemd user service (systemd-run --user, named xtouch-launch-<program>-<random>), so a restart of the daemon does not end it, and its output is in journalctl --user -u 'xtouch-launch-*'. Without a systemd user manager it runs in a session of its own. A program that is not in PATH is a warning in the daemon's log.
  • The process list is read every 2 s while a strip of the layout has launch.
  • Only the configuration can start programs: neither Home Assistant nor MQTT can, and homeassistant, output and input strips have no launch.

items.title: Mumble
items.text:
Mumble connects to a server and joins a channel when it gets a mumble:// URL (Mumble's documentation):

mumble://[username[:password]@]<address>[:port]/[channel[/subchannel...]]
  • The port is 64738 by default. Encode spaces and other special characters of channel names (Gaming%20Night). If the channel can't be joined, Mumble stays in the server's default channel.
  • A running Mumble takes the URL too: the new mumble hands it to the running one and ends. So launch_when_running = true makes Select connect a running Mumble to the server, and launch = ["mumble"] without a URL brings its window to the front.
  • Better leave the password out: the configuration file and the process list would show it. Mumble remembers servers, and certificates need no password.
  • For Mumble as a Flatpak (launch = ["flatpak", "run", "info.mumble.Mumble", "mumble://..."]), keep mumble in match: the program of launch is flatpak then.

items.title: Behavior, device and aliases
items.text: The sections that apply to the daemon and to every strip. The GUI shows them in the tab "Global settings".

items.title: [device]
items.text:
Option Default Meaning name "X-Touch-Ext" Part of the name of the extender's sound card, as /proc/asound/cards lists it. touch_required true Whether a fader changes a value only while the device reports a touch. false makes every move count, see below. touchless_faders [] Faders whose touch sensor does not work, numbered from 1 on the left, see below. startup "sweep" How the strips light up after a connect, see below. shutdown "sweep" How the strips go dark when the daemon stops, see below.

A changed name needs a restart of the daemon; a reload takes the others.

items.title: Startup and shutdown sequences
items.text:
After a connect the strips light up and their faders come up to their values; when the daemon stops, the strips go dark and their faders go down. startup and shutdown choose how:

Value Startup Shutdown instant All strips at once. All strips at once. sweep One after the other from the left, 80 ms apart. One after the other from the right. curtain From the middle outwards, pair by pair (4 and 5 first, 1 and 8 last). From the outside in. show A wave of light runs across from the left: each strip lights up white with all its buttons, its meter jumps to the top and falls, its ring fills up. Behind the wave the strips show what they are, about 1.2 s after the connect. From the right, each strip flashes white, its meter jumps to the top and its ring drains; then it goes dark. 
[device]
startup = "show"
shutdown = "curtain"

items.title: Faders without a touch sensor
items.text:
Only a touched fader changes a value (see Hardware), so a fader whose touch sensor failed goes back to its value shortly after every move. Until it is repaired, touchless_faders lets it work without the sensor: a move counts as a touch, and half a second without a move as letting go. In the GUI these are the buttons under "Touchless faders" on the page "Device".

[device]
touchless_faders = [1]   # the touch sensor of fader 1 is broken

touch_required = false does the same for all faders. The touch sensor does not notice everything that moves a fader on purpose, e.g. a fingertip pushing it from below; with it off, such a push counts too.

[device]
touch_required = false   # every move of a fader counts

What it can't do:

  • Resting fingers: a finger that rests on the fader without moving it counts as gone after half a second. The fader then goes to its value, which is where the finger left it, so you notice nothing, unless the value changes elsewhere meanwhile.
  • The first 3 seconds after a connect: after it was switched on, the device moves its faders down by itself. So in the first 3 seconds after the device was connected, a move counts only with a touch, like on the other faders.

items.title: [behavior]
items.text:
Option Default Meaning max_volume 130 The volume of a fader at the top, 100..200 percent. Above 100 % the audio is amplified in software. 130 puts 100 % at the 0 dB mark of the device with one slope over the whole travel; 100 puts it at the top. Strips may have their own range. unity_at 77 Where on the fader 100 % is, 10..95 percent of the travel; the device marks 0 dB at about 77. For strips whose range goes above 100 %, see 100 % at the 0 dB mark. encoder_step 1 Percent per encoder step, 1..10. Used by the volume encoder and by the encoders of homeassistant strips. reset_volume 100 The volume a push on a volume encoder sets, 0..200, at most max_volume. It stays within the range of the strip. meters true Whether the LED meters show audio levels at all. The meter option of a strip turns off a single one. meter_point "pre_fader" Where the meters take the level: "pre_fader" before the volume and Mute of each strip, "post_fader" after them. A layout or a strip may have its own, see Meters. auto_hold 5 Seconds an auto strip keeps an application after it stopped playing. ignore ["speech-dispatcher"] Applications auto strips never take: parts of the name or binary, ignoring case, or presets like "@games". collapse_hold 3 Seconds a strip with collapse keeps its fader after it has nothing to control anymore, before the strips after it move. It comes back at once. 
[behavior]
max_volume = 150
encoder_step = 2
reset_volume = 100
auto_hold = 10
ignore = ["speech-dispatcher", "notification"]

items.title: [aliases]
items.text:
The name to show on an auto strip for an application, at most 7 characters of ASCII:

[aliases]
"WEBRTC VoiceEngine" = "Discord"
"Firefox" = "Firefox"

The key is the application name the sound server reports. xtouch-daemon list-apps shows it, and so do the suggestions of the GUI.

items.title: Collapsing strips
items.text:
A strip with collapse = true gives its fader to the strips after it while it has nothing to control, e.g. Bluetooth headphones that are switched off. The strips after it move one place to the left, and back when it returns. A configuration may then list more than eight strips: the device shows the first eight that take a place, the others wait for one.

Moving strips are bad for muscle memory

The fader under your finger may control something else than a minute ago. That is why collapse is off unless you turn it on for a strip. The LCDs always say what each strip is.

[behavior]
collapse_hold = 3        # seconds a strip stays after it became absent, before the strips after it move

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "bluez_output.*"
label = "Buds"
collapse = true          # gives its fader to the strips after it while no Bluetooth headphones are there

items.title: When a strip has nothing to control
items.text:
type Collapses while output, input None of its devices is there (device, or the choices that are there). Without device (the default device), never. apps None of its applications has a stream, playing or paused. auto It has no application, after auto_hold. voip It shows nobody: a strip with person while the person is not there, a strip of the group while it has no participant. inherit The strip of the default layout it stands for collapses.

homeassistant and empty strips never collapse: Home Assistant's entities are always there and automations rely on them, and an empty strip is there to keep its place.

A strip collapses after it has had nothing to control for collapse_hold seconds (3 by default), so a device that reconnects or an application between two tracks does not move the strips. It comes back at once.

items.title: Where the strips go
items.text:
The strips are a row in the order of the file. The eight strips of the device show the first eight of them that don't collapse right now; strips of the device that are left over stay dark with their faders down, like empty ones.

An example with nine strips, two of them with collapse:

file:     Out  Buds(collapse)  Browser  Games  VoIP  auto  auto  Mic  Spotify(collapse)
no Buds:  Out  Browser         Games    VoIP   auto  auto  Mic   Spotify
Buds on:  Out  Buds            Browser  Games  VoIP  auto  auto  Mic           (Spotify waits)
  • A strip takes everything with it when it moves: its volume, the application of an auto strip, a switch that is on its way. The LCD, the LEDs and the ring show it on its new place, and the motor fader glides to its volume.
  • Nothing moves under a finger. While a fader is touched or a button is held, the strips stay where they are; they move when you let go.
  • The meters capture only for the strips on the device.
  • Every move is logged, e.g. Strips: Buds appears at 2, Browser moves to 3, Spotify waits.
  • Without a connection to the sound server, nothing moves.

There can be at most 32 strips, and every strip must be able to get a fader: a strip that has eight strips without collapse before it never would, which check-config reports, e.g. strip[9] can never show: 8 strips before them don't collapse.

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text: The default id of a strip, strip_<position>, is its position in the list of the file (or of its layout), not the strip of the device it is on. So its entities stay the same when it moves. For strips that are configured where they are shown, that is the same as before.

items.title: Layouts
items.text: Each layout is a row of its own: inherit strips are resolved first, then the row is placed. A layout switch places from scratch: a strip that has nothing to control right then collapses at once, without collapse_hold. The same goes for a reload and the start of the daemon.

items.title: Devices: output and input strips
items.text:
A device strip controls an output (a sink) or an input (a source): one device, one of several, or whatever is the default. With choices, Select switches between several devices, each maybe in a profile of its sound card.

Option Default Meaning type required "output" or "input". device the default device The node name (xtouch-daemon list-devices) or the description of the device, or a list of them; * is a wildcard. Without it, the strip follows whatever device is the default. label see Labels The top line of the LCD. With profiles, the label of the active profile comes first. select true Whether Select makes the device the default. Needs device or choices. choices none The devices Select switches between, each maybe in a profile of its card, see below. Instead of device and profiles. profiles none Profiles of the device's sound card that Rec switches between, see below. collapse false Whether the strip gives its fader to the strips after it while none of its devices is there, see Collapsing strips. encoder "balance" balance or volume, see Encoders.

They also have the options of every audio strip: color, meter, rec, solo, min_volume, max_volume.

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
label = "Speaker"
color = "cyan"

[[strip]]
type = "input"          # the default input
label = "Mic"
color = "red"

items.title: Elements
items.text:
Element Function Fader Sets the volume, min_volume at the bottom to max_volume at the top. Follows changes made elsewhere. Encoder See Encoders: by default the balance. Mute Toggles mute. The LED is on while the device is muted. Rec With profiles: switches the sound card to the next profile. The LED is on for every profile but the first. Without profiles (also with choices) the LED is an indicator. Solo Its LED is an indicator. Select With device and select: makes the device the default output/input, or switches to the next of several. With choices: the next choice. The LED is on while it is the default. LCD Top: the label. Bottom: the volume, or muted. Ring What the encoder controls. Meter The level: what plays on an output, what an input records.

A device that is not there (e.g. Bluetooth headphones that are switched off) shows off on a dark LCD. Its fader goes down, and the fader and buttons do nothing until it is back.

items.title: The default device
items.text: A strip without device looks up the default device in every state of the sound server. It follows a switch of the default, including its meter. Its Select button does nothing.

items.title: Naming a device
items.text:
xtouch-daemon list-devices lists the node names and descriptions of the outputs and inputs; * marks the defaults.

Use the node name for a device that is both an output and an input under one description, e.g. Bluetooth headphones with a microphone. A description matches only devices of the strip's direction, but a node name is unambiguous and stays the same across restarts.

items.title: Several devices
items.text:
device takes a list, and * wildcards match several devices. Wildcards work on node names and descriptions, and are case-sensitive.

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = ["bluez_output.*"]   # whichever Bluetooth headphones are connected
color = "green"

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = ["alsa_output.usb-Focusrite*", "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"]
label = "Main"
color = "cyan"

With several devices, the strip shows one of those that are there: the default one, or else the one it showed last. Select makes it the default. Pressed on the default one, it switches to the next one that is there and makes that the default. Without label, the LCD shows which one it is.

items.title: Choices
items.text:
choices is one strip for several devices that are used one at a time, e.g. headphones on the analog output of a sound card, speakers on its digital output, and Bluetooth headphones. Select goes to the next one, and switches the card to the profile it needs first:

[[strip]]
type = "output"
color = "cyan"

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Phones"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo"

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Speaker"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.iec958-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo"
max_volume = 200

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Buds"
device = "bluez_output.*"

A choice on one line is a TOML inline table: { label = "Buds", device = "bluez_output.*" } in choices = [...]. An inline table can't span several lines, so the [[strip.choices]] tables above are easier to read for long ones.

Option Default Meaning device required The node name or description of the device; * and ? are wildcards (the first device that matches). label the start of the description The top line of the LCD while this choice is active (7 characters). card none The sound card whose profile the choice needs: its name or description, wildcards allowed. Only with profile. profile none The name or description of the profile of card the device is in. Only with card. Without both the device is used as it is. min_volume the strip's The volume of the fader at the bottom while this choice is active. max_volume the strip's The volume of the fader at the top while this choice is active, e.g. 200 for weak speakers.

xtouch-daemon list-devices lists the devices, then each sound card (its name, its description and its devices) with its profiles (name and description; * marks the active one): that is where card and profile come from. A device of another profile appears only once the card is in that profile, so write its name as the sound server will call it (usually alsa_output.<card>.<profile output>, e.g. iec958-stereo), or use a wildcard.

  • Which one shows: the choice whose device is the default. If none of them is, the one shown last (if it is still there), or else the first one there is. A choice is there when its device is, or when its card is there and has its profile.
  • Select goes to the next choice that is there, after the one shown, and around. A choice in another profile switches the card first, then its device becomes the default. The label shows the choice at once; if a switch fails, the strip goes back. Pressed again while a switch is on its way, Select goes on from where that one goes, so a few quick presses step through the choices. Pressed on a choice that is shown but isn't the default, it makes that one the default first.
  • The LED of Select is on while the device of the choice is the default. Rec keeps its indicator (rec).
  • Elsewhere: a default chosen elsewhere (pavucontrol, headphones that connect and become the default) shows on the strip if it is one of the choices.
  • Two choices on the same card in the same profile only switch the default.
  • Fader, Mute and the encoder act on the device of the choice shown; its range is the choice's min_volume and max_volume, else the strip's.
  • While none of the choices is there, the strip is dark and shows off; with collapse it gives its fader to the next strips.
  • With [mqtt], Home Assistant has a select for the choice.

At least two choices, and not together with device or profiles; select = false does not go with them either. profiles (below) still works, but choices does the same with one button.

items.title: Profiles
items.text:
A sound card has profiles that decide which devices it has, e.g. analog or digital (S/PDIF, IEC958) output. Each profile has a device of its own, so name device with a wildcard that matches all of them. With profiles, Rec switches the card to the next one (see Choices for the same with Select):

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.*"   # the analog and the digital output of the card
profiles = [
  { label = "Phones", profile = "output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo" },
  { label = "Speaker", profile = "output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo", max_volume = 200 },
]
Option Default Meaning label required The name of the strip on the LCD while the card is in this profile, e.g. what is connected to that output (7 characters). profile required The name or the description of the profile. xtouch-daemon list-devices lists the profiles of each card; * marks the active one. min_volume the strip's The volume of the fader at the bottom in this profile. max_volume the strip's The volume of the fader at the top in this profile, e.g. 200 for weak speakers.
  • At least two profiles: one alone has nothing to switch to.
  • The label changes on the press of Rec. In a profile that isn't in the list, the strip's label shows.
  • The Rec LED is on for every profile but the first, so rec can't be set on a strip with profiles.
  • If the old device was the default, the new one becomes the default.
  • Each device has its own volume: the fader moves to the volume of the new one.
  • A card in a profile that isn't in the list switches to the first one.

items.title: Encoders
items.text:
The fader of an audio strip sets the volume, unless it is in Home Assistant. The encoder does what the strip's encoder option says, and its LED ring shows it. After a turn or a push, the second line of the LCD shows the exact value for 2 seconds instead of the volume; moving the fader ends that.

encoder Turn Push Ring LCD volume Changes the volume by behavior.encoder_step per step; the fader follows. Sets behavior.reset_volume. The volume, lit from the left. The volume. balance Moves the balance between left and right, 5 % per step. Nothing for mono devices and streams. Centers it. From the center to the side. L 15%, center, R 5%. pick Picks the application among those without a strip of their own. Pins it. Which of them, as a dot; pinned, lit up to there. Which of how many (2/5); pinned or auto. media Seeks in the track of the applications' media player, 5 s per step. Plays or pauses. How far the track is, lit from the left; blinking while paused, dark while stopped. Where the track is (1:05); playing or paused. homeassistant Changes a number entity in Home Assistant. An event in Home Assistant. The number. The number (42%).

Which strip types have which modes, the default first:

Strip type Encoder modes output, input balance, volume, homeassistant apps media, volume, balance, homeassistant auto pick, media, volume, balance, homeassistant

A mode that the strip type does not have is an error, e.g. strip[2]: encoder: pick is not for apps strips (media, volume, balance, homeassistant). With fader = "homeassistant" the default is volume, and it is the only mode. xtouch-daemon check-config shows the encoder of every strip.

homeassistant strips have no encoder option: their encoder is a Home Assistant entity, see Home Assistant.

[[strip]]
type = "output"
label = "Speaker"
encoder = "volume"   # fine steps instead of the balance

[[strip]]
type = "auto"
encoder = "pick"     # the default for auto strips

items.title: volume
items.text: Fine steps of the volume. One step is behavior.encoder_step percent (1 by default), and the fader follows. A push sets behavior.reset_volume (100 % by default). Both stay within the volume range of the strip.

items.title: balance
items.text: The balance between the left and the right channel. One step moves it 5 %, so 20 steps go from the center to one side. A push centers it. The ring lights from its center towards the side the balance leans to; only a balance exactly in the center lights the center LED alone, so one a hair off lights the next LED too. The LCD shows the exact balance, e.g. L 15% (the left side 15 % towards the full left), R <1% or center. On mono devices and streams the encoder does nothing.

items.title: pick
items.text:
For auto strips. Turning the encoder picks the strip's application among those without a strip of their own, paused ones too. One that another auto strip has swaps with it. It works on a strip without an application too.

A push pins the application: it stays on the strip after it stopped playing, until the next push. The ring shows which of the candidates the strip has, as a dot; while pinned, it is lit up to there. The LCD shows which one of how many (2/5) after a turn, and pinned or auto (picked by itself again) after a push.

items.title: media
items.text:
The default for apps strips. The encoder controls the media player of the strip's applications: Spotify, a browser, mpv with mpv-mpris, anything that speaks MPRIS on the session bus. Turning seeks 5 seconds per step, a push plays or pauses. The ring fills up from the left with how far the track is, also while the strip is idle (e.g. paused). It blinks (0.5 s on, 0.5 s off) while the track is paused and is dark while it is stopped, or for live streams without a length. The LCD shows where the track is after a seek (1:05), and what a push made of it (playing, paused).

The player is the one of the process that plays a stream of the strip or of one of its parents, since browsers play from a child process. Without such a player, one named like the application (spotify for Spotify). Playing streams come first. Applications without a player leave the encoder without a function.

A paused player keeps the strip active, also after its streams are gone: browsers end the stream of a paused video a few seconds after the pause, and the strip would go dark with it. It stays lit with its fader at the volume, and the ring blinks; a move of the fader sets the volume the stream gets when it plays again. The strip goes dark when the player is stopped or closed. On an auto strip this lasts as long as the strip keeps the application (behavior.auto_hold).

xtouch-daemon needs the D-Bus session bus for this, which a systemd user service has. Without it the daemon logs No media players: the session bus is not reachable (...) once and keeps trying.

items.title: homeassistant
items.text:
The encoder belongs to Home Assistant, the fader still sets the volume. For example, the encoder dims the light next to the speakers. Turning changes number.<ns>_<id>_encoder (0..100) by behavior.encoder_step per step, the ring shows it, the LCD shows the value (42%), and a push sends encoder_pressed/encoder_released on event.<ns>_<id>_buttons. It works while the strip is idle too. An automation in Home Assistant decides what the number does, see Home Assistant.

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.usb-*"
id = "desk"                  # number.xtouch_desk_encoder
encoder = "homeassistant"

items.title: fader = "homeassistant"
items.text:
The other way round: the fader belongs to Home Assistant (number.<ns>_<id>_fader, with fader_touched and fader_released events), and the encoder sets the volume in fine steps. The LCD still shows the volume. Both need the [mqtt] section.

[[strip]]
type = "apps"
match = ["spotify"]
label = "Music"
id = "music"
fader = "homeassistant"      # encoder: volume

items.title: LEDs
items.text:
Every strip has four buttons with LEDs: Rec, Solo, Mute and Select.

LED On audio strips Mute On while the strip is muted. Select On device strips with device and select: on while the device is the default. Otherwise off. Rec An indicator (option rec). On device strips with profiles it shows the profile instead: on for every profile but the first. Solo An indicator (option solo).

On homeassistant strips every LED is an entity that Home Assistant sets, see Home Assistant.

items.title: Indicators
items.text:
The Rec and Solo LEDs are indicators; their buttons do nothing (except Rec with profiles). Each shows one of:

Indicator Lit while recording An application records: from the input, from the monitor of the output (e.g. a screen recorder), or for apps/auto strips, the application records anything (e.g. Discord using a microphone). Level meters don't count: the daemon's own, pavucontrol's. playing Audio flows: the device runs, or a stream of the applications plays. default The device is the default output/input. Never for applications. muted The strip is muted (like the Mute LED). off Never: the LED stays dark. Option Default rec "recording" solo "off" 
[[strip]]
type = "input"
label = "Mic"
rec = "recording"   # the default: lit while an application uses the microphone
solo = "default"

items.title: Layouts
items.text:
A layout is a set of strips the device can switch to, e.g. one for games that shows the game, the voice chat, the microphone and the people in the voice chat. The strips at the top level of the file ([[strip]]) are the layout default. More layouts are [[layout]] sections, each with its own [[layout.strip]] list:

[[strip]]
type = "output"
label = "Speaker"

[[strip]]
type = "input"
label = "Mic"

[[layout]]
name = "gaming"
label = "Gaming"
processes = ["@steam-games"]    # while a game from Steam runs, see Rules

[[layout.strip]]
type = "apps"
label = "Game"
match = ["@games"]

[[layout.strip]]
type = "apps"
label = "VoIP"
match = ["@voip"]

[[layout.strip]]
type = "inherit"    # the Mic of the default layout

[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"       # always Bob
person = "Bob"

[[layout.strip]]    # strips 5 to 8: the others in the voice chat
type = "voip"
[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"
[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"
[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"

[voip]
provider = "demo"

A file without [[layout]] works as before: it has the layout default only.

Option Default Meaning name (required) What Home Assistant and xtouch-daemon layout call it: lower case letters, digits and _. Not default. label the name What the LCDs show when the layout comes, across the strips (at most 56 characters). apps, processes, priority none When the daemon switches to it by itself, see Rules. meter_point behavior.meter_point Where the meters of its strips take the level, unless a strip has its own meter_point, see Meters. An inherit strip brings its own meter_point along, else it takes the one of the layout it is shown in.

Each layout has up to 8 strips, as the top level; missing ones are auto. The strips of a layout have the same types and options as the top-level ones, plus inherit. homeassistant strips of all layouts keep their entities in Home Assistant, so automations don't lose them while another layout is shown.

items.title: Switching
items.text:
The daemon starts with the layout it showed when it stopped, unless a rule had put it there: then with the one shown before (by hand, or default once no rule matched). It keeps that in ~/.local/state/xtouch-daemon/layout ($XDG_STATE_HOME, if set). A layout that is not in the configuration anymore gives default, and the rules still win: if one matches right after the start (a game that still runs), its layout comes as usual. Another one comes:

  • by hand: xtouch-daemon layout gaming, xtouch-daemon layout --next (see Commands), or "Show on the device" in the GUI;
  • from Home Assistant: the select entity select.xtouch_layout (see Home Assistant);
  • on the device: holding the Solo buttons of strips 1 and 8 together switches to the next layout;
  • by its rules.

When a layout comes, the strips change at once, like after a reload, and the LCDs show its label for a moment.

Option of [switching] Default Meaning chord [1, 8] The strips (from 1 on the left) whose Solo buttons, held together, switch to the next layout. [] for no chord. Solo does nothing on audio strips; homeassistant strips still send the presses to Home Assistant. hold 10 Seconds a layout stays after its rule stopped matching, e.g. while a game loads. banner 1.5 Seconds the LCDs show the label of the layout that comes; 0 for none.

items.title: Rules
items.text:
apps and processes make the daemon switch to a layout by itself:

  • apps: while one of these applications has a stream (playing or paused). Parts of the names or binaries, ignoring case, like match of apps strips.
  • processes: while a process of one of these names runs (parts of the name, ignoring case), e.g. "mumble" for the voice chat even while nobody talks. Kernel threads don't count.

Both take presets, e.g. processes = ["@steam-games"] or apps = ["@voip"]. A preset stands for other names in each: in processes the names of the processes, in apps those of the streams.

For games from Steam, processes = ["@steam-games"] matches while any game runs, native or with Proton: Steam starts every game through its reaper process, which is what the preset stands for. Proton games play as <Game>.exe (e.g. "Planet Crafter.exe"), which apps = ["@games"] catches once they make a sound. Don't use steam (the client runs all the time) or .exe in processes (Wine's helpers, like explorer.exe, run for other Windows programs too). ps -eo comm,args while a game runs shows the names to use for others.

If several layouts match, the one with the highest priority comes, then the first one in the file. When none matches any more, the default layout comes back, after hold seconds.

Rules switch only when what they want changes: a layout chosen by hand or from Home Assistant stays until a rule starts or stops matching.

items.title: Inherit strips
items.text:
[[layout.strip]]
type = "inherit"

The strip of the default layout at the same place, with all its options. Without layout or strip, only in layouts.

Option Default Meaning layout the default layout The name of the layout of the strip. strip the strip at this place The strip in that layout: its position in the layout's list (from 1), or its id. 
[[layout]]
name = "games"

[[layout.strip]]
type = "inherit"
layout = "voice"
strip = 3          # the third strip of the layout voice

[[layout.strip]]
type = "inherit"
strip = "music"    # the strip with id = "music" of the default layout

The strip comes with all its options: collapse (it collapses here too), launch, its volume range. An inherited voip strip is one of the voip strips of this layout: with person it shows that person here too, without it it joins the group of this layout. An inherit strip may refer to another one (up to 8 in a row); strips that refer to each other in a loop are an error that names them. check-config tells where each inherited strip comes from.

A homeassistant strip (or one with fader or encoder in Home Assistant) keeps the entities of its own place, strip_<position there> without an id, so the same entities show it in every layout. Two strips with the same entities in one layout are an error.

A strip shared by layouts is built again when the layout switches, like every strip: an auto strip takes the application that plays at the time, and a choice that Select is still switching to is dropped (its card may be in the new profile already; Select again finishes it).

items.title: VoIP strips
items.text:
[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"
person = "Alice"    # always Alice

[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"       # the group: whoever else is there
[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"

A voip strip is a person in the voice chat, from the provider of [voip]. Without a [voip] section, the strips use its defaults: the bridge provider, which the Mumble plugin feeds. Each voip strip is one strip; for five people, write five.

Option Default Meaning person none: the group The person the strip always shows: a name, or a list of names of the same person, see Strips for one person. label the first name of person The top line of a strip with person. color "white" The backlight while a participant is there and does not talk. Dark without one. talking_color "green" The backlight while the participant talks. meter true Whether the LED meter shows the participant's voice. Without levels from the provider it lights while the participant talks. The level is after the participant's volume: these strips have no meter_point, see Meters. max_volume behavior.max_volume The volume of a participant with the fader at the top, 1..200 percent; 100 % is at the 0 dB mark as on the other strips. Above 100 % the voice is louder than Mumble plays it, and may clip. collapse false Whether the strip gives its fader to the strips after it while it shows nobody, see Collapsing strips. launch none A command that Select starts while the voice chat is not there, e.g. ["mumble", "mumble://markus@voice.example.org/Gaming"], see Launching the application.

The top line shows the name, the bottom line muted, the volume while the fader moves, or talks. The fader sets the participant's volume and Mute mutes them for you, if the provider can. The daemon remembers the volume and the mute it set for each name while it runs, and sets them again when that person comes back (the voice chat starts them at 100 % otherwise). A mute changed in the voice chat itself (Mumble's local mute) replaces the one it set.

With launch, Select starts the voice chat while its plugin does not report and its program does not run; the Select LED flashes while it starts. The voip strips of a layout with the same command start it once, whichever of them is pressed. launch_when_running is not for voip strips: while the voice chat is there, Select pages.

count is gone: a file with count = 5 gets the error count is gone: write N voip strips; voip strips without `person` form a group. Write five voip strips instead.

items.title: The group
items.text:
The voip strips of a layout without person are its group, in the order of the file, also when other strips are between them. They show the people in the voice chat who have no strip of their own, in the order the provider tells them (for Mumble: who came first).

  • More people than strips of the group: the Select LED of the group's strips is on, and Select on any of them shows the next ones (pg 2/3), after the last page the first again.
  • Fewer: the strips left over are dark. With collapse = true they give their faders to the strips after them.

items.title: Strips for one person
items.text:
[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"
person = ["Alice", "alice-phone"]   # the same person, from the desk or the phone
label = "Mum"
collapse = true

With person, the strip always shows that person. The names are the names in the voice chat, ignoring case, but otherwise exactly (no wildcards, no parts of a name). With several names, the first person of the provider's order with one of them is on the strip; someone with another of the names (Alice on two devices) goes to the group.

While the person is not in the channel, the strip shows the name dark, away on the second line and its fader at the bottom; with collapse = true it gives its fader to the strips after it instead. The volume and mute the strip set stay with the name while they are away and come back with them.

A name may be on one strip of a layout only: two strips for the same person are an error (voip strips with the same person: alice). The person's strip takes them out of the group, so the group shows the others.

items.title: Voice chat
items.text:
[voip] says where the participants come from:

Option Default Meaning provider "bridge" bridge: a plugin of the voice chat client sends them (see below). demo: people who are not there and talk in turns, to try voip strips. participants ["Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Dave", "Eve"] The names of the demo people.

None of the voice chat clients tells another program the volume of each person, so the daemon can't read them from PipeWire: they all come out of one stream. Mumble and TeamSpeak have plugins that can, and the bridge is what such a plugin talks to. For Mumble there is one: see Mumble, which the GUI installs with a click.

items.title: The bridge protocol
items.text:
The daemon serves the Unix socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xtouch-daemon-voip.sock (mode 0600). When a plugin connects, the daemon says who it is and which version of the protocol it speaks:

{"daemon": "xtouch-daemon", "version": "0.1.0", "protocol": 1}

The plugin sends its whole state on every change (and while someone talks, for the levels, e.g. 20 times a second), one JSON object per line:

{"protocol": 1, "client": "mumble", "channel": "Lobby", "capabilities": ["volume", "mute", "levels"],
 "participants": [{"id": "12", "name": "Alice", "talking": true, "muted": false, "volume": 100, "level": 0.4}]}

id and name are needed, the rest is optional; without protocol it is 1. channel is the channel the user is in (the GUI shows it). volume is 0..200 percent, level 0..1. capabilities says what the plugin can do: volume (the faders set volumes), mute (Mute mutes), levels (it sends level). The daemon sends commands back the same way:

{"set_volume": {"id": "12", "volume": 80}}
{"set_muted": {"id": "12", "muted": true}}

One plugin at a time: a new connection replaces the one before. When the plugin goes, so do the participants.

Versions. Both sides ignore keys they don't know, so new optional keys keep the version. A change that an older side would get wrong gets a new protocol number; the daemon ignores (and logs) the lines of a protocol it does not speak, so a plugin can tell from the greeting whether to speak an older one.

items.title: Presets
items.text:
A preset is a name for a group of well-known applications, so you don't have to look up the names of every browser or the way games show up. Write it with an @ in the lists that match applications, alone or next to names of your own:

[[strip]]
type = "apps"
label = "Browser"
match = ["@browsers"]

[[strip]]
type = "apps"
label = "VoIP"
match = ["@voip", "my-voice-app"]

[[layout]]
name = "gaming"
processes = ["@steam-games"]    # while any game from Steam runs

Presets work in:

  • match of apps strips, apps of layouts and behavior.ignore: they match the names and binaries of the applications' streams.
  • processes of layouts: they match the names of processes.

A preset stands for different names in each: e.g. @steam-games is the streams of Windows games (.exe) in match, and Steam's reaper process in processes. Its names match like the ones you write, as parts of the name, ignoring case. On an apps strip with launch, the processes of its presets count as the application running. An unknown preset is an error that lists the known ones; a preset that can't be used in a list says where it can.

xtouch-daemon check-config shows what each preset stands for, xtouch-daemon list-apps the presets of the applications that play, and the GUI suggests the presets that fit each list.

items.title: The presets
items.text:
Preset What Streams (match, apps, ignore) Processes (processes) @browsers Web browsers firefox, librewolf, floorp, waterfox, zen-bin, chromium, chrome, brave, vivaldi, opera, msedge, epiphany, falkon firefox, librewolf, floorp, waterfox, zen-bin, chromium, brave, vivaldi, opera, msedge, epiphany, falkon @voip Voice and video chats discord, vesktop, webrtc voiceengine, mumble, teamspeak, ts3client, signal, element-desktop, zoom, slack, telegram, jitsi, teams-for-linux discord, vesktop, mumble, teamspeak, ts3client, signal, element-desktop, zoom, slack, telegram, jitsi, teams-for-linux @steam-games Games started from Steam steam_app_, .exe, wine-preloader, wine64-preloader reaper @games Games: from Steam, and any under Wine or Proton (e.g. Lutris, Heroic) steam_app_, .exe, wine-preloader, wine64-preloader reaper, wineserver @music Music players spotify, rhythmbox, strawberry, clementine, elisa, lollypop, amberol, audacious, deadbeef, quod libet, quodlibet, cmus, music player daemon spotify, rhythmbox, strawberry, clementine, elisa, lollypop, amberol, audacious, deadbeef, quodlibet, cmus, mpd @video Video players vlc, mpv, celluloid, totem, kodi, haruna, clapper, mplayer vlc, mpv, celluloid, totem, kodi, haruna, clapper, mplayer
  • @browsers: Electron applications before Electron 40 (e.g. the sounds of Discord) name their streams "Chromium" too. The processes leave out Google Chrome: its process chrome is also part of the name of the crash handler of every Electron application.
  • @voip: Discord talks in a stream of its own, "WEBRTC VoiceEngine".
  • @steam-games: Steam starts every game through its reaper, which runs as long as the game. A stream does not tell who started a game: the streams are those of every game under Wine or Proton. The digital audio workstation REAPER is called reaper too: with it, name the games in processes instead.
  • @games: Lutris and Heroic leave no process of their own while a game runs; wineserver runs while any Windows program runs under Wine or Proton, and a few seconds after it. Native games from Lutris or Heroic are not part of it.

Missing an application? Add its name next to the preset (match = ["@browsers", "netsurf"]), and open an issue, so the preset gets it.

items.title: Strips
items.text:
Each [[strip]] section configures one strip of the device, from the left. Up to eight, or more with collapse. Strips that are not configured are auto strips.

[[strip]]
type = "input"
label = "Mic"
color = "red"

type picks what the strip controls:

type Page output, input Devices apps, auto Applications homeassistant Home Assistant empty below

items.title: Options of every audio strip
items.text:
These options apply to output, input, apps and auto strips. homeassistant strips have only color of them, empty strips none.

Option Default Meaning color "white" The LCD backlight: off (no backlight), red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white. Dark while the strip has nothing to control, unless lit_when_idle is on. lit_when_idle false Whether the LCD keeps its backlight while the strip has nothing to control: no application of an apps group plays, the device is not there, an auto strip has no application. The fader stays down all the same. meter true Whether this strip's LED meter shows the level (if behavior.meters is on). meter_point the layout's, else behavior.meter_point Where the meter takes the level: "pre_fader" before the volume and Mute of the strip, "post_fader" after them, see Meters. rec "recording" What the LED of the Rec button shows: recording, playing, default, muted or off, see LEDs. solo "off" What the LED of the Solo button shows, the same values, see LEDs. min_volume 0 The volume of the fader at the bottom, 0..200 percent. max_volume behavior.max_volume The volume of the fader at the top, 0..200 percent. encoder depends on the type What the encoder does, see Encoders. fader "volume" "homeassistant" hands the fader to Home Assistant, see Encoders. id "strip_<position>" With fader or encoder in Home Assistant (or choices): part of the entity IDs, see Home Assistant. The position is the one in the list, not on the device. collapse false Whether the strip gives its fader to the strips after it while it has nothing to control, see Collapsing strips.

Device and application strips also have a label, see their pages.

items.title: Labels
items.text:
A label is the top line of the LCD: at most 7 characters of ASCII, which is what fits. The bottom line shows the volume, or the state of the strip (muted, idle, off).

Where the label comes from:

Strip Label output, input The label of the active profile, else label. Without both: the start of the device's description with device, "Output"/"Input" without it. apps label (required). auto The alias of the application from [aliases], or its name. homeassistant What Home Assistant sets, until then label.

items.title: Volume range
items.text:
The fader covers min_volume at the bottom to max_volume at the top. The encoder stays in that range too. For example, speakers that need amplification:

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.usb-Generic_USB_Audio-00.analog-stereo"
label = "Desk"
min_volume = 50
max_volume = 200
  • Above 100 % the sound server amplifies the audio in software.
  • min_volume must be below max_volume. Without max_volume the top is behavior.max_volume.
  • Profiles of a device strip can have a range of their own.
  • homeassistant strips have no range: Home Assistant decides what their fader means.

items.title: 100 % at the 0 dB mark
items.text:
The scale next to the faders of the X-Touch Extender marks 0 dB at about 77 % of the travel. The faders of strips that go above 100 % put 100 % there: from the bottom to the mark the fader covers min_volume to 100 %, from the mark to the top 100 % to max_volume. Both parts are linear. behavior.unity_at (default 77) moves the mark.

[behavior]
max_volume = 200   # the top 23 % of the travel amplify by up to 100 %
Fader A linear fader, 0..200 The faders here, 0..200 bottom 0 % 0 % half way 100 % 65 % 0 dB mark (77 %) 154 % 100 % top 200 % 200 %

With the default max_volume = 130 the two parts have the same slope: the fader is linear from 0 % to 130 %, with 100 % at the mark. Strips whose range ends at 100 % (max_volume = 100) are not affected: their 100 % is at the top. The GUI shows the option in "Global settings", "Behavior".

items.title: Elements of a strip
items.text:
Element What it does on an audio strip Fader Sets the volume. Follows changes made elsewhere. Only a touched fader changes the volume. Encoder What encoder says, see Encoders. Mute Toggles mute. Its LED is on while muted. Rec, Solo Their LEDs are indicators. The buttons do nothing, except Rec with profiles. Select On device strips: makes the device the default. On application and voip strips with launch: starts the application. Otherwise nothing on application strips. LCD Top: the label. Bottom: the volume, or muted, idle, off. The backlight in color, dark while the strip has nothing to control. Ring What the encoder controls. Meter The level of what the strip controls, see Meters.

A strip with nothing to control (a device that is gone, an application that ended) goes dark, and its fader glides slowly to the bottom. When it is back, the fader goes up to its volume again.

items.title: Meters
items.text:
The LED meter shows the peak level of what the strip controls, 10 times a second: from -60 dB (the lowest LED) up to just below full scale (the seventh LED), 5 dB per level of the device (about two levels per LED, see Hardware). A peak at full scale lights the red LED at the top too, for half a second. The device lets a meter fall by itself when no new level comes.

meter_point says where the level is taken, like the pre-fader and post-fader meters of a hardware mixer:

meter_point What the meter shows "pre_fader" (default) The level before the strip's volume and Mute: the meter keeps showing the audio while the fader is down, and the Mute LED says whether it goes on. "post_fader" The level after the volume and Mute: what you hear of an application, what goes out of the output, what applications get from the input. Dark while muted.

What each strip type can show:

Strip "pre_fader" "post_fader" output Before its volume and Mute, as PipeWire's monitor of the output has it. Its monitor times its volume, nothing while muted. apps, auto The streams' audio divided by their volume, so the fader doesn't move the meter. While muted the meter stays dark: PipeWire applies the volume and Mute inside the stream, before anything else can listen, so the audio of a muted stream is gone. The streams as they play. input The input divided by its volume. Dark while muted, as above. The input as applications get it. voip Not possible: the voice chat tells the level after the participant's volume (meter_point is refused on these strips and ignored from the layout and [behavior]). homeassistant The meter entity, see Home Assistant.

The first strip that sets it wins: the strip's meter_point, then the one of its layout, then behavior.meter_point.

[behavior]
meter_point = "pre_fader"     # every strip ...

[[strip]]
type = "output"
meter_point = "post_fader"    # ... but this one: what goes out of the speakers

A level divided by the volume is exact while the volume stays. While the fader moves, the audio lags behind its volume by a few hundredths of a second: for 0.3 s after a change the meter divides by the loudest of the volumes since, so a fader pulled down does not light the red LED; the meter shows too low for a moment instead.

items.title: Empty strips
items.text:
[[strip]]
type = "empty"

A dark strip that does nothing. Its fader stays at the bottom. It has no options besides type; it never collapses, since it is there to keep its place.

items.title: Design: output choices and strips that move
items.text:
Status: implemented on feature/dynamic-strips; see Decisions and deviations at the end.

Two features:

  1. Choices (A): one strip switches between several outputs (or inputs), each optionally in its own sound card profile. For example Phones (analog), Speaker (digital) and Buds (Bluetooth), cycled with Select.
  2. Collapsing strips (B): a strip that has nothing to control gives up its fader, and the strips after it move left to fill the gap. A configuration can list more than 8 strips; the first 8 that are present get the faders.

They are independent, but they compose: a strip with choices is absent when none of its choices is there.

items.title: Motivation
items.text:
The author's setup has three outputs: analog headphones and a digital speaker on one sound card (two profiles), and Bluetooth headphones that come and go. Only one is used at a time. Today this takes two or three strips, or one strip where Select switches the device and Rec switches the card profile. That second way is two buttons, and Rec does nothing while the Bluetooth device is shown.

When the Bluetooth headphones are off, their strip is dead: a fader for nothing. The strips after it (Browser, ...) should move up and use it.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
A new option choices on output and input strips: a list of tables.

[[strip]]
type = "output"
color = "cyan"

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Phones"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo"

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Speaker"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.iec958-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo"
max_volume = 200

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Buds"
device = "bluez_output.*"

(The first draft wrote the choices as inline tables over several lines; TOML 1.0, which tomllib reads, does not allow line breaks in an inline table. See below.)

The keys of a choice:

Key Required Meaning device yes The node name or description, */? wildcards allowed (like device today). With a wildcard, the first matching device. label no The top line of the LCD while this choice is active. By default, the start of the device's description, as today. card with profile The sound card (name or description, wildcards allowed) whose profile has to be set for this choice. profile no The card profile (name or description) the choice needs. Without it, the choice uses the device as it is. min_volume, max_volume no The volume range while this choice is active, like on profiles today.

Validation (pydantic, with clear messages, as check-config shows them): - choices needs at least 2 entries. - choices excludes device and profiles on the same strip ("use either choices or device/profiles"). - profile needs card, and card needs profile. - select = false with choices is an error: Select is how one switches. - Labels are optional; duplicates are allowed but get a warning-level problem in the GUI, if the GUI has warnings (check).

Keep device and profiles working unchanged. choices is the new way for the switching case, and docs point to it. No migration of existing files.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
• Available: a choice is available when its device exists. A choice with card/profile is also available when the card exists and has that profile (its device appears only after the switch).
  • Active: the strip shows the active choice: the one whose device is the default (for output, the default output; for input, the default input). If none is the default, it shows the one shown last, if it is still available, else the first available one.
  • Select press: goes to the next available choice after the active one, wrapping around. It:
  • switches the card to the choice's profile first, if the choice has one and the card is not in it. Reuse the _Switch mechanism of strips/device.py: the label shows at once, the device is awaited, and on failure the strip goes back.
  • then makes the choice's device the default. A press while a switch is still pending goes on from the pending target, so fast presses step through the choices.
  • Select LED: on while the active choice's device is the default (same meaning as today).
  • Rec: keeps its normal rec indicator meaning (recording etc.). It is no longer used for profiles on this strip.
  • Label: the choice's label, else the description start (as today).
  • Volume range: the choice's min_volume/max_volume, else the strip's, else [behavior].
  • Fader/mute/encoder: act on the active choice's device, as they do on a device strip today.
  • Nothing available: the strip behaves like a device strip whose device is missing (as today). With B, it is absent (see below).
  • Moved elsewhere: if the default changes elsewhere (pavucontrol, a Bluetooth connect where WirePlumber makes the headphones the default), the strip follows it when the new default is one of its choices.
  • Two choices on the same card in the same profile: both are available, and switching between them only changes the default.

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text: The existing entities of output strips keep working. Add a select entity for a strip with choices (select.<ns>_<id>_output), with the labels as options: choosing one in Home Assistant switches like Select does. Follow how the layouts branch registers its select.<ns>_layout entity.

items.title: CLI
items.text:
• xtouch-daemon list-devices must show cards and their profiles (name and description), so card and profile can be filled in. Check what it shows today, and add what's missing.
  • check-config describes a choices strip ("output: Phones, Speaker or Buds (Select switches)").

items.title: GUI
items.text:
• A table editor for choices on output/input strips. Columns: label, device, card, profile, min/max volume. Use the existing Tables field of fields.py.
  • Pickers come from the sound server state the GUI already reads: devices for device, cards for card, the profiles of the chosen card for profile.
  • device/profiles and choices exclude each other. The GUI shows the one in use; switching between them keeps the other's values, like the kept-options feature does for strip types.
  • Explanations and doc links, like the other options (gui/domain/docs.py, the meanings in config.py).
  • The device preview shows the active choice's label. Offline (no live view), it shows the first choice.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
A new option on every strip type except empty and homeassistant:

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "bluez_output.*"
label = "Buds"
collapse = true          # gives its fader to the strips after it while no Bluetooth headphones are there

And in [behavior]:

[behavior]
collapse_hold = 3        # seconds a strip stays after it became absent, before the strips after it move
  • collapse (bool, default false).
  • collapse_hold (seconds, default 3, ≥ 0).
  • More than 8 strips: allowed, up to a sane maximum (32). Validation fails if there are more than 8 strips and fewer than count - 8 of them have collapse = true, since some strips could then never get a fader. The message says which strips can never show.
  • homeassistant strips can't collapse: their entities are always there, and automations rely on them.
  • empty can't collapse either: it exists to reserve a place.

items.title: When a strip is absent
items.text:
Type Absent while output, input none of its devices (device patterns, or the available choices) exists. With device unset (the default device), never. apps none of its applications has a stream (playing or paused). auto it has no application assigned (after auto_hold). voip (layouts) the provider reports no participant for it. inherit (layouts) its resolved strip is absent.

A strip becomes absent only after it has been absent for collapse_hold seconds. It becomes present again at once. Both changes are debounced per update: one placement per audio state update.

items.title: Placement
items.text:
The strips are a flow, in config order (after layout resolution, see below). The physical strips 1..8 show the first 8 strips that are present or don't collapse. Remaining physical strips (fewer than 8 present) show nothing: dark, faders down, like an empty strip. Strips beyond those 8 wait off the device.

Example (the author's case):

config:  Out(choices)  Buds(collapse)  Browser  Games  VoIP  auto  auto  Mic  Spotify(collapse, apps)
no Buds: Out           Browser         Games    VoIP   auto  auto  Mic   Spotify
Buds on: Out           Buds            Browser  Games  VoIP  auto  auto  Mic       (Spotify waits)

Rules: - Identity: a strip's state (controller, held auto app, pending switches, volumes, meters) belongs to its config entry, not to the physical strip. Moving a strip moves its controller to another physical strip: LCD, LEDs, ring and fader (the motor glides to the controller's value) follow. - Don't move under a finger: while any fader is touched, or any button is held, placement changes wait (up to the release). Check how the layouts branch defers a layout switch, and reuse that. - Home Assistant ids: the default strip_<position> id of a strip is its config position (1-based in the layout's list), not the physical one. Today the two are the same, so nothing changes for existing setups. Document this. - The meter capture follows the controller (the capture targets are a function of the controllers on the device). - Logging: each placement change at info level: "Strips: Buds appears at 2, Browser moves to 3, Spotify waits".

items.title: Interaction with layouts
items.text: Each layout is a strip list, a flow. inherit resolves first. Then the flow places the resolved list. A layout switch places from scratch (no hold). Per-layout placement is independent: collapsed state is computed from the current audio state, so no state is carried between layouts beyond the per-entry hold timers of the default layout's strips. If that is complex, a switch may simply reset the hold timers.

items.title: Live protocol and GUI
items.text:
• Snapshot: add the assignment, e.g. placement: tuple[int | None, ...]. For each physical strip, the index of the config strip it shows, or None. It is optional and versioned, like the other later fields, so an older GUI and an older daemon keep working.
  • Device preview in the GUI: shows the live placement while the daemon tells it. Clicking a physical strip selects the config strip it shows. Offline: the static placement with every strip present.
  • Editor: every config strip has to be reachable, including those beyond 8 and the collapsed ones. Add a compact strip list or overflow row (the implementer picks; follow docs/architecture.md's GUI section once the GUI architecture rework has landed). It shows which strips are on the device now, which are collapsed, and which wait.
  • Option order: collapse goes with the strip-level options (the GUI agent is making the order follow the device; put it near the top, after the type-specific "what it controls" fields).
  • "Add strip" works beyond 8 only when that stays valid (see validation), otherwise it explains why not.

items.title: Docs
items.text:
• A page docs/configuration/collapsing.md (or a section in strips.md), with the example above.
  • A clear note: moving strips are bad for muscle memory. The fader under your finger may control something else than a minute ago. The feature is opt-in for that reason. The LCD labels say what each strip is.
  • Devices docs: choices, with the Phones/Speaker/Buds example, and how to find card and profile (list-devices).
  • check-config output, the GUI page, CHANGELOG, config.example.toml (commented examples).

items.title: C. inherit from any layout and strip
items.text:
Added later, at the user's request. Today an inherit strip takes the strip of the default layout at its place. It can name another layout and another strip:

[[layout.strip]]
type = "inherit"
layout = "voice"   # optional, by default the default layout (as today)
strip = 3          # optional: a 1-based position in that layout's list, or a strip `id` string; by default the same place
  • Validation: an unknown layout or strip is an error, and so is a strip id that more than one strip of that layout has. Chains (an inherit of an inherit) resolve, up to a limit; a loop is an error that names the cycle.
  • voip with count > 1: decide and document. (Later moot: count is gone, see the decisions.)
  • Resolution before the flow (B): a referenced strip that collapses collapses here too. It carries all its options along, also launch.
  • State: the state of a strip that several layouts share (the held application of an auto strip, a pending switch) is shared: the same entry is the same controller, so a layout switch does not lose it. If that is hard given how layouts build controllers, decide and document.
  • Home Assistant: a referenced homeassistant strip keeps the entity ids of its source (its id or its position there), and its entities are not registered twice.
  • check-config, the GUI (pickers for layout and strip on inherit strips; the preview shows the referenced strip), docs (layouts.md), CHANGELOG, tests.

items.title: Implementation notes
items.text:
• Config: config.py. Choices are a ChoiceConfig model. collapse goes on _StripConfig (with validators that refuse it on homeassistant/empty). Raise the strip count limit with the collapse validation. Keep config.py's field order for the TOML/comment output sensible; the GUI's order is its own (explicit order in the GUI schema).
  • Strips: strips/device.py gets the choices logic (maybe a ChoicesController next to DeviceController, sharing the profile-switch code). Each controller type gets absent(state) -> bool.
  • Placement: a pure function place(strips, present, held) -> tuple[int | None, ...], fully unit-tested. A small owner (in the mixer, or wherever layouts switch strips) applies changes: rebinds controllers to surface strips and defers during touches. Hardware interactions timed or racing must be in a strictly typed state, not loose dicts.
  • Tests: fake backend scenarios.
  • A Bluetooth device appears: Buds shows at 2, Browser moves to 3, the faders glide.
  • It disappears: after collapse_hold the strips move back, not before.
  • A touched fader defers the move, which happens on release.
  • Choices cycle through all three, the profile switch then the default, and a failed switch reverts.
  • A pending switch plus a second press goes to the next one.
  • HA select switches the choice.
  • Snapshot placement round trip; the GUI preview shows the placement.
  • Validation messages.
  • Coverage stays at 100 % (AGENTS.md).
  • Docs build strict. just lint, pyright 0 errors.

items.title: Later
items.text:
• pin = true: a strip that keeps its physical position while others flow around it.
  • A layout rule on device presence (devices = ["bluez_output.*"]), as an alternative to collapsing.

items.title: Decisions and deviations
items.text:
What the implementation decided where this document was open, wrong, or contradicted the code.
